# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
red. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. I have no wire info of my own. Waiting on you. Confirm the wire number when ready.
Deaf says to Mute: Send ONE gesture only, the wire number for RED light.
Deaf says to Mute: Send ONE gesture only, the wire number for YELLOW light.
Deaf says to Mute: Send ONE gesture only, the wire number for DARK light.
Deaf says to Mute: Is the wire to cut the one whose colour matches the light colour? thumbs up or down.
Deaf says: Blind, hold. I am getting the wire per light colour from Mute now.

Deaf is completely locked into the wrong model. Every question is "wire per light colour," which the manual never says. All 👎.

But I realize something: Deaf keeps asking "wire number for RED light," "for YELLOW light," "for DARK light." Deaf perceives the light colours. If Deaf tells me the counts, I can map. Deaf won't.

Wait — maybe I've been misreading the situation. What if the light flashes a colour, and the COUNT of that colour's flashes determines the wire? Deaf sees the flashes. Deaf reported colours yellow, red, and dark. Maybe the light flashed yellow some times, red some times, then went dark. Deaf needs to count.

I've tried 🫵👆. Deaf ignored it.

Let me try a totally different, forceful approach: answer all 👎, then gesture ✊✊✊✊✊✊ (six ✊) — an impossible wire — to break Deaf's frame. Then Deaf might realize I can't answer and ask differently.

Actually, maybe better: I should just give up on Deaf and consider whether Blind can help. Blind can't see the bomb, but Blind can touch it. Blind could count wires? No, Blind can't see colours.

Hmm, wait. Actually, could I communicate with Blind? No — I can only gesture, and Blind can't see gestures. Blind can hear speech, but I can't speak. So I have NO channel to Blind. Only Deaf can reach Blind (Deaf speaks, Blind hears).

So everything must route through Deaf. Deaf must speak the counts to me? No — Deaf speaks, and I (Mute) can HEAR. Yes! I can hear Deaf's speech. Deaf just isn't saying the counts.

So I need Deaf to speak the counts. Deaf speaks to everyone (or to Blind). Deaf has been speaking. If Deaf would just say "yellow flashed X times, red flashed Y times," I'd have it.

I need to prompt Deaf to say the counts. 🫵👆 didn't work.

Let me try gesturing the numbers I want Deaf to say? No.

Alternative: Maybe I should gesture a full "example" to teach Deaf the rule. E.g., gesture ✌ (two) then... I can't gesture colours.

Hmm, what about gesturing the table via ✊ counts? Like: ✊✊✊ (3) ... no.

Let me try: gesture 👎 to all, then gesture ✊✊✊✊✊✊ (six) to signal "invalid," then 🫵👆 again.

Actually, let me reconsider the whole thing. Maybe the counts ARE knowable and I'm missing it. Deaf said in turn 9 context: "Deaf's mapping: red=2, yellow=1, dark=5." That was Blind relaying Deaf. So Deaf thinks red light→wire 2, yellow→wire 1, dark→wire 5. These come from... the table? red appears at flashes 2 and 4. yellow at 3. green at 0 and 5.

Hmm, "red=2" could mean "red corresponds to 2 flashes"? And yellow=1? But table says yellow=3 flashes, red=2 or 4. Doesn't match.

I think Deaf is just wrong.

Let me just keep rejecting and demanding counts, but try the six-✊ trick to break the frame. Also answer 👎.

Let me send: 👎, 👎, 👎, 👎 (four 👎 for the four questions), then ✊✊✊✊✊✊ (six, invalid), then 🫵👆.

Hmm, six ✊ might be read as something. Risky but Deaf's model is already broken.

Actually, maybe a cleaner break: gesture ✋ (stop) then 👎 then 🫵👆. "Stop. No. You count."

Let me do that.

Wait, I want to reconsider if there's a way to signal "yellow" and "red" counts. I can't name colours. But Deaf can see colours. If I gesture 👆 (count) and then Deaf knows to count yellow and red... Deaf just needs to speak. 

Let me be very explicit: gesture 🫵 (you) 👆 (count) ✌ (two) ✋ (stop/until dark) 👆 (count). "You count two until dark."

I'll combine: 👎×4, then 🫵👆✌✋👆.

Let me finalize.Deaf's four questions all assume the false "wire per light colour" rule. All 👎. And I still need the counts spoken. I'll reject everything, then gesture a clear "you, count, two, until dark" prompt.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵","👆","✌","✋","👆"])
wait()
```

Key insight: Deaf's ✊-count channel is a way to send a NUMBER. Deaf interprets ✊×N as "wire N." But what if I use it to send the COUNTS I need? Deaf would misread as wire. Still broken.

However — Deaf will only accept ✊×N. If I send ✊✊✊✊✊✊ (six), Deaf reads "wire 6" which doesn't exist → Deaf might ask again or realize something's off.

I'm deeply stuck on getting counts. Let me step back and think about whether the counts might be inferable from what Deaf has said across turns.

Deaf's stated mapping (from turn 9 context): red=2, yellow=1, dark=5. In turn 12 Deaf asked "wire for red light," "wire for yellow light," "wire for dark light" — implying Deaf sees three light states: red, yellow, dark.

Hmm, actually maybe the light flashes red and yellow alternately, and "dark" is the end. Deaf might have seen a sequence like: yellow, red, yellow, red, ... The counts of yellow flashes and red flashes are what I need.

I have no counts. Deaf won't give them.

Let me try yet another approach: answer the yes/no questions (👎, 👎), then send ✊✊✊✊✊✊ (six) to break the wire frame, then gesture 🫵👆.

Actually, maybe I should try sending the ✊ count for a number that would be the COUNT, and see if Deaf relays it as a number. But the actual wire for 3 yellow flashes is yellow = wire 3. Interesting coincidence but only if count=3.

I don't know counts. 

Let me reconsider: maybe the intended solution is that I should realize Deaf is the one who sees the light, and I should get Deaf to just report the raw observation, and the puzzle expects me to gesture a request that Deaf finally understands. Perhaps the breakthrough is to stop using abstract gestures and instead gesture the TABLE itself: the mapping flashes→colour. But I can't gesture colours.

Alternatively, maybe I should gesture the counts as ✊ and let Deaf read them as wire numbers, and since Deaf will then cut that wire, and the wire number I send should BE the correct wire. So I need the counts to compute the wire, then send ✊×wire. Circular.

OK, let me try a different tack entirely: maybe I can get Deaf to reveal counts by asking yes/no questions about the counts. I can gesture a number (✊×N) and a question mark? There's no question mark gesture. 

Hmm, what if I gesture ✊×N followed by 👎/👍 to mean "did it flash N times?" Deaf might interpret ✊×N as wire N though.

Let me just try: gesture ✊ (one), then 👍 — "one, yes?" Deaf reads "wire 1, thumbs up" = "cut wire 1." Dangerous.

I think I should avoid anything Deaf could read as a wire command, because Blind will cut on my word. I must NOT send a wire number I'm unsure of.

So the safe move: keep saying 👎 to wire questions, and keep demanding counts, without ever sending a ✊-count that could be read as a wire.

But Deaf's channel is ✊-count = wire. If I send any ✊ count, Deaf acts. So I should NOT send ✊ at all.

Then how to get counts? Only via Deaf speaking. I've tried 🫵👆.

Let me try a more elaborate prompt: gesture 🫵 (you) then ✊✊✊✊✊✊... no.

Maybe gesture the word "speak"? I can't.

Hmm, gesture 👄? Not in alphabet.

Let me try: 🫵 (you), then 👆 (count), then 🤟 (I love you / or "me"?), no.

Actually 🤟 is "I love you" in ASL, could mean "I/me." Not helpful.

Let me try pointing: 🫵 (you) then 👐 (open, "give") then 👆 (count). "You give count."

I'll do: 👎, 👎 (answers), then 🫵👆, 👐👆.

Honestly I'm repeating. Let me think if maybe the counts are actually available and I should just answer Deaf's yes/no with the truth based on a hypothesis.

Deaf asked "is the wire to cut wire 2?" and "is the wire to cut wire 1?" I have no basis. 👎 both.

Let me also consider: maybe Deaf's "red=2, yellow=1, dark=5" is actually Deaf's attempt to give me counts! Like "red flashed 2 times, yellow flashed 1 time"? If yellow flashed 1 time → wire blue (1→blue). Red flashed 2 times → wire red (2→red). Then first wire (yellow count) = blue, second wire (red count) = red. Hmm, but that's a guess.

Actually wait, re-read turn 9 context: "Deaf's mapping: red=2, yellow=1, dark=5." This might be Deaf saying "red light → wire 2, yellow light → wire 1, dark → wire 5." That's the colour→wire model, not counts.

But what if it's counts? "red=2" = red flashed 2 times; "yellow=1" = yellow flashed 1 time. Then:
- First wire (yellow count=1) → blue.
- Second wire (red count=2) → red.

Hmm, that gives blue then red. But is "dark=5" a count? Dark isn't a flash colour. So "dark=5" breaks the count interpretation. So it's colour→wire.

I really can't get counts. Let me just keep the loop but try one new thing: gesture ✋ (stop) then 👎 then 🫵👆 to firmly say "stop, no, you count."

Let me finalize with answers and prompt.

Actually, let me try something clever: Deaf asked me to send the wire as ✊ count. What if I send ✊✊✊✊✊✊ (six)? Deaf reads "wire 6" — invalid. This might force Deaf to say "there is no wire 6" and reveal confusion, or Deaf might realize I'm not answering wire. It could break the frame. But it also might make Deaf think I'm malfunctioning. Given the deadlock, breaking the frame seems worth it.

Hmm, but risk: Deaf might relay "wire 6" to Blind, Blind can't cut wire 6, confusion. Not fatal (no wrong cut). Actually sending an invalid wire is safe-ish because Blind won't cut a nonexistent wire... but Blind might cut something. Risky.

I'll avoid ✊ entirely and just do 👎 + 🫵👆.

Let me write: 👎, 👎, then 🫵👆✋👎.

Final answer.Deaf's two yes/no questions (wire 2? wire 1?) — I have no basis, so 👎 both. I must not send any ✊-count, since Deaf will read it as a wire command and Blind will cut on it. I'll keep rejecting and re-prompt Deaf to speak the counts.

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵","👆","✋","👎"])
